io_driver_functions.notes: Raw DMA3 serial-bit transfer primitive over EEPROM bus 0x0D000000; writes src/dst/count|enable into DMA3-adjacent MMIO globals and busy-waits bit 15 of a status halfword before returning. Shared by both read and write paths; has no other callers in the 241-function corpus.

EEPROM block READ. Bound-checks block address against max block count, clocks out a READ command + address bitstream via FUN_08118df0, clocks in 0x44 (68) response bits, unpacks into 4 big-endian u16 halfwords into caller-supplied buffer. Sole caller is the write-verify function FUN_08119094 (no separate 'load into game state' reader was found in this workspace).
Thin wrapper: calls FUN_08118f34(param_1, param_2, 1) with the wait-for-ready flag fixed to 1.

EEPROM block WRITE (raw hardware). Packs 4x u16 payload + block address MSB-first into a serial bitstream, clocks it out via FUN_08118df0, then polls the EEPROM ready bit (uRam0d000000 & 1) in a timeout loop (threshold 0x88 ticks) before returning. No application-level checksum logic present; the poll loop is purely a hardware write-completion wait.

Write-verify: reads back the just-written block via FUN_08118e70 and compares each of 4 halfwords against the original payload; returns 0 on match, 0x8000 on first mismatch. This is the ONLY integrity mechanism found in the traced corpus -- a hardware read-back-and-compare, not a stored/software checksum field. Labeled role=checksum here because it is the closest functional analogue present; there is no stored checksum byte range in the save file.

Top-level write/verify/retry entry point: loops up to 3x calling FUN_08118f20 (write) then FUN_08119094 (verify), breaking on clean verify. Confirmed via exhaustive scan of every function's callees list in ghidra/callgraph.json to have ZERO callers in the 241-function decompiled corpus. This is the highest save-writer function visible in this workspace; the game-logic call site that triggers it is outside the traced function set and is reported as UNKNOWN.
